_: rules.json — every decision Rushes makes about media lives here, and nowhere else.
_why: There are two builds of this app: PHP for a NAS, Python for everything else. If either
one decides things in its own code, they drift apart and the app develops two
personalities. So: build layers know about HTTP and files. This file knows about media.
If you are about to write an 'if' that decides something about a file, it belongs here.
Edit it freely — nothing here is code, and your camera or editing suite may differ.

kinds._: Extension → what sort of thing it is. Used for the search filter chips.

_: Folder names that describe the camera or the card, not the shoot. When working out
(Every camera names the folders inside DCIM three digits and five characters —
100CANON, 100MSDCF, 100NIKON, 100GOPRO — which is the second pattern below.)
what a file belongs to, these are stepped over. Matched whole, case-insensitively.
A folder that is just a year is skipped too — that rule is in 'structure' below.

system_junk._: Never indexed, never counted, never moved. The OS and the NAS make these.

_: Editing scratch that regenerates itself from the originals. Large, worthless,
and safe to move out — but only what genuinely rebuilds.
'sweep' is offered for removal. 'keep' is reported and never touched.

keep.label: Premiere auto-save
keep.why: This is what you open when a project will not. Never swept.

structure._: How a file's owner and event are worked out from its path.

trees.archive: source material, by date and event. Video, audio and stills together.
trees.projects: the job: editing projects, graphics, exports.
trees.library: reusable material: logos, fonts, templates, music.

_: A duplicate is content, never a filename. Cameras reuse names, so every card
starts at 0001 again and name matching finds coincidences, not copies.
duplicates.compare: size, then first and last megabyte on a size collision

_: When the same file is in several places, one copy is kept and the others are moved
aside. These copies are never the one kept, whatever else is chosen: a higher
number weighs more. 'contains' is a piece of the path; 'matches' is a pattern
(awk). Folders that only one archive has go in its settings.json, set in Setup.

rules.why: the recycle bin: deleted on purpose
a copy someone made of a folder
a file saved twice with its extension doubled

_: What the admin screen is allowed to say, and when. A condition appears only when
it is true. Levels: good, info, warn, bad. Sizes are in bytes.

analysis._: Describing footage. themes: the only words a shot's themes can be, one to three per shot. Edit freely; shots described before a change keep their old themes until described again.
